references.text: The instructions for making the incense to be used in the sanctuary, which is what fills the golden bowls mentioned in Num 7:86.
The definition of the sanctuary shekel, which is the unit of weight used to measure the golden bowls.
The golden bowls (kappot) made for the tabernacle, the same type of vessels mentioned here filled with incense.
The first time a golden bowl filled with incense is mentioned in the chapter, when Nahshon from the tribe of Judah brought his offering.
Nethanel from the tribe of Issachar brought a golden bowl weighing ten shekels and filled with incense, following the same pattern summarized in verse 86.
Golden bowls filled with incense in heaven, symbolizing the prayers of the saints, parallel to the incense offering in the tabernacle.
Incense brought before the golden altar in front of the throne, linking the tabernacle's incense offering to heavenly worship.
